reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous reasoning to identify initial patterns in shared features with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and validate spurious correlations. This ensures both high-level pattern detection and rigorous attribution-based evidence for spurious features. The combination increases confidence in identifying truly shared and misleading features that are not semantically relevant to the target variable.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are present in both instance A (13590) and instance B (5730), and determine if any feature is common across all misclassified instances (even if not listed).
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features between the two instances, including any that might be consistently present across all misclassified cases.

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, relationship=Husband) could serve as a spurious correlate—despite having no direct causal link to income—by analyzing its potential for correlation with predictions.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A rationale for why a shared feature might be spurious, especially if it appears frequently in misclassified instances but lacks semantic relevance to income prediction.

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides a global, interpretable view of feature importance across all instances, helping detect shared high-impact features. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local and gradient-based attributions to confirm whether a feature drives misclassification. Sensitivity analysis isolates the feature's impact by reducing its value, testing whether misclassification persists—distinguishing true spuriousness from real signal. Together, these tools validate whether a shared feature has high attribution despite being semantically unrelated.
